# AGENTS.md — Build, Test, and Validation Commands
# Auto-generated by spec-to-ralphprep v1.0.0 — Project: ai-accounting-hub

## Environment
```bash
cp .env.example .env   # fill in values before first run
```
Required env vars (full list + descriptions in .env.example):
DATABASE_URL, NATS_URL, TEMPORAL_HOST, QBWC_USERNAME, QBWC_PASSWORD,
QBWC_ENDPOINT_URL, SWARMSYNC_API_BASE_URL, SWARMSYNC_SA_API_KEY,
VCAP_SHARED_SECRET, AIVS_SIGNING_KEY_PATH, INVOICEPROOF_WEBHOOK_SECRET
AIHUB_OUTBOX_TOKEN, SYSTEM_A_CALLBACK_TOKEN. Set SYSTEM_A_URL explicitly, or
on Railway ensure the peer-service variable RAILWAY_SERVICE_EXEMPLARY_TENDERNESS_URL
is present so System B can normalize it and deliver bill-synced callbacks.

## Install
```bash
python -m venv .venv && . .venv/Scripts/activate   # POSIX: . .venv/bin/activate
pip install -r requirements.txt
```

## Database (canonical store = Supabase Postgres; NATS+Temporal local)
```bash
docker-compose up -d        # NATS + Temporal only (Postgres is Supabase-managed)
alembic upgrade head        # run migrations against Supabase DATABASE_URL
python scripts/seed.py      # seed dev data
alembic downgrade base      # reset (dev only)
# Alt: apply migrations via the `supabase-aihub` MCP (apply_migration)
```

## Development Server
```bash
uvicorn app.main:app --reload --port 8000
# Operator dashboard (server-rendered, shadow mode): http://localhost:8000/ui
# Requires jinja2 (in requirements.txt) for the /ui templates.
```

## Test
```bash
pytest -q                   # unit tests
pytest -q -m integration    # integration tests
pytest -q                   # all tests (ralph's gate — must exit 0)
```

## Lint / Type Check
```bash
ruff check .
mypy app
```

## Build (production)
```bash
docker build -t ai-accounting-hub .
```

## Validation Gate (ralph runs this after every task — must exit 0)
```bash
ruff check . && mypy app && pytest -q
```
Runs: (1) lint, (2) type check, (3) unit + integration tests.

## Daily digest email (app/integration/daily_digest.py)

Satisfies spec-stv-integration-layer-2026-06-29.md §16 / DoD condition #10
("Daily digest email: delivered to Ben's inbox with correct content from
staging."). Read-only aggregation over the canonical store (System B) plus,
optionally, System A's `integration_outbox` — renders the fixed
"STV Integration Health — YYYY-MM-DD" plain-text template with an
auto-generated Action items list, then sends it via **stdlib `smtplib`**.

**No new dependency was added** — `requirements.txt` is unchanged;
`smtplib` / `email.message.EmailMessage` are Python stdlib.

New `Settings` fields (`app/config.py`), all optional (no startup
enforcement — the digest is schedulable/optional, not a hard boot
dependency; missing config raises only when `send_digest_email()` is
actually called):
- `smtp_host`, `smtp_port` (default 587), `smtp_username`, `smtp_password`
  (never logged), `smtp_use_tls` (default `True`)
- `digest_email_from`, `digest_email_to` (Ben's inbox — set via env, e.g.
  Railway `SMTP_HOST`, `SMTP_PORT`, `SMTP_USERNAME`, `SMTP_PASSWORD`,
  `SMTP_USE_TLS`, `DIGEST_EMAIL_FROM`, `DIGEST_EMAIL_TO`)

Manual trigger:
```bash
python -m app.integration.daily_digest
# or, with a System A outbox handle for real outbox counts:
python -m app.integration.daily_digest --system-a-database-url "postgresql://..."
```
This is a plain callable (`send_daily_digest`) + CLI entrypoint only — no
scheduler/cron framework was added (no APScheduler/Celery beat/GitHub
Actions cron exists anywhere else in this repo, so none was introduced
here per "smallest correct change"). Wiring a recurring trigger (Railway
cron, Temporal schedule, etc.) is an explicit follow-up; DoD #10 requires
only that the email delivers correctly from staging, not that it runs on
an automatic timer yet.

Known approximation: no Temporal workflow-listing API exists in this
codebase, so "Temporal: N active workflows, N escalated (>48h)" is
approximated via `bills.status='verified'` (the state where a workflow is
blocked on the human approval signal) — documented in the module
docstring and in `_aggregate_temporal_proxy`.

## Phase 6 — QBWC write-back live-session wiring (task 9/10/11)

The write-back adapter (`app/transport/qbwc_writeback.py`) is now wired into the
live QBWC SOAP session (`app/transport/qbwc.py`). A `QBWCSessionManager`
constructed with a `WritebackConfig` runs a WRITE phase after the two read
stages: it drains `bills` that are `status='approved'` AND proof-passed and emits
`BillAdd`, driving each bill through the existing `sync_bill_to_qb` (proof
boundary re-checked directly against the DB before every write — fail closed).
When no `WritebackConfig` is supplied the session is exactly the original
READ-ONLY state machine, so the connector handshake is unaffected.

New modules:
- `app/transport/qbwc_resolution.py` — canonical→QB reference resolution
  (vendor `qb_list_id`, cost-code→account FullName, class, Customer:Job, Draw #,
  fee-role→policy Dr account). Unresolvable *required* ref → `EntityResolutionError`
  (fail closed; the session marks the bill `status='exception'`, never guesses).
- `BillWriteDriver` (in `qbwc_writeback.py`) — bridges `sync_bill_to_qb`'s
  synchronous `writer(request)->response` to QBWC's split sendRequestXML/
  receiveResponseXML poll cycle via a short-lived per-bill worker thread (NOT a
  poller/listener: it lives only for one bill inside one handshake, fed only by
  the outbound-poll callbacks, joined on completion). Reuses the proof-boundary,
  session-gap, and 3200 EditSequence retry logic verbatim.
- `mark_bill_exception(...)` — fail-closed handler used by the session on an
  unresolved entity.

Draw/fee bills (`bills` rows with `draw_package_id` + `raw_extensions.fee_role`)
route through the SAME `BillAdd` write path, each gated by the same
approved+proof-passed check.

New tests: `tests/test_qbwc_resolution.py` (13), `tests/test_qbwc_write_stage.py`
(7) — DB + QBWC writer both mocked, real qbXML codec exercised end-to-end.

No new runtime dependencies (uses stdlib `queue`/`threading` only) — requirements.txt
unchanged. Full E2E against a real Rightworks QuickBooks session remains Section 10
of spec-qbwc-writeback-adapter-2026-07-01.md (blocked on the sandbox .QBW file).
